month_theme: IB done. Duke committed. Gap year application due June 1.

must_do.text: Duke Gap Year Program application — finalize and submit before June 1. This is the highest-priority item of the week.
Duke housing and orientation registration — complete any outstanding enrollment steps regardless of gap year outcome.
Update your career coach — your plan was built around Northwestern. Duke changes the course sequence, project teams, and some timelines. Say 'update my plan' to walk through it.

should_do.text: Gap year activity planning — finalize the phase structure: scuba certification (Coiba), glider project, FAA Private Pilot Certificate, Mongolia service (Summer 2027). Lock in any that have registration deadlines.
Begin C++ and Calculus BC self-study — these are in the gap year plan and compound over time. Start this week even if lightly.
Rest and decompress properly. The IB is done. Take at least 2-3 days before going full throttle on planning.

could_do.text: Research Duke Pratt first-year ME course sequence and identify aerospace-relevant student teams (AERO, rocketry, design-build-fly).
Draft a short introduction email to 1-2 Duke ME or AE faculty doing propulsion or dynamics research. Send in June.

key_dates.event: Duke Gap Year Program application deadline — 8 days away
Duke housing preferences deadline (if not taking gap year)

notes: The IB is finished. You committed to Duke. The gap year application is due June 1 — 8 days away. That is the only hard deadline this week and it needs to be done before anything else. Duke housing registration is a parallel must-do regardless of gap year outcome. Your career plan was built around Northwestern's specific course sequence, project teams, and timeline — it needs to be updated to reflect Duke and the potential gap year. Talk to your coach to revise it. Everything else this week is planning and setup.
